summary: Angelina County tower listed as gone in the FFLA index; a March 2026 Texas Highways article places a 100-foot fire tower on the Texas Forestry Museum grounds in Lufkin.

facts.status_note: FFLA index marks the original Lufkin tower Gone; Texas Highways (2026) describes a 100-foot fire tower standing on the Texas Forestry Museum grounds in Lufkin

access.note: Tower altered to keep climbers off it (Bowman, weekly column dated 2010-02-28, updated 2012-12-06); the museum's indoor exhibits are free to the public (Texas Highways, 2026)

corrections.why: Texas Highways (March 2026) describes a 100-foot fire tower standing on the Texas Forestry Museum grounds in Lufkin; the FFLA index marks the original site Gone

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The FFLA index marks the Lufkin tower Gone but gives no site description, and Texas Highways (2026) describes the tower standing on museum grounds. The story reports it as relocated and standing at the museum, and says the index does not specify which location it means.

notes_for_editor: Brief status 'gone' is contradicted by Texas Highways (March 2026), so status is set to relocated (see corrections). Build year is in conflict: Texas Highways gives 1936 and says the tower came from the Conroe area, while Forest Lookouts quotes a March 1974 item that says a 100-foot tower 'will be built' on the proposed museum site. The story reports both and does not choose. Bowman's page says towers 'such as the one at Lufkin' were built by the CCC in 1936; that is a general statement, so it is not used for the build date. The FFLA index also lists a Conroe (Jones Forest) tower as gone, but no source ties that site to this tower, so it is not used. The Lufkin Daily News article (a search snippet says the museum no longer lets visitors climb the tower) returned HTTP 429 and was not read, so the climbing point rests on Bowman's column (dated 2010-02-28, updated 2012-12-06), which is not recent and does not say when the tower was altered. Height 30.5 m is the brief value; 100 ft is 30.48 m. Budget: 1 WebSearch, 4 successful page reads, 2 failed (429 and 403).
